title: Interleaved Canary Windows & Stakeholder Ops Hub
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We frequently run overlapping canary windows across runtime, console, and API surfaces for different feature rollouts. That creates notification fatigue, unclear ownership during escalations, and difficulty understanding cumulative customer exposure. This initiative will build an "ops hub" and scheduling model that allows interleaved canaries to be coordinated, visualized, and automatically routed to the right on-call/stakeholder lanes.
goals: Single-pane visualization of all active and upcoming canary windows across runtime/console/api
Automated stakeholder routing and escalation for overlapping rollouts based on tag/impact
Reduce on-call interruption noise by 40% during multi-surface deploy weeks
Provide preflight checks that block new canaries if exposure thresholds are exceeded
scope_in_scope: Design and deliver an ops-hub UI in the Console showing canary timelines and collision warnings
Standardize canary metadata schema (impact, owners, fallback variants, rollback runbook link)
Server-side scheduler that enforces non-overlap or soft-prioritization policies per team/priority
Notification templates and escalation rules integrated with PagerDuty and Slack
scope_out_of_scope: Implementing new deployment systems (we will integrate with existing deploy hooks)
Changing lower-level runtime kernel scheduling or autoscaling logic (unless critical blockage found)
Audit log retention/archival policy changes (separate compliance project)
milestones: 2026-03-15: Finalize canary metadata schema and owner model
2026-03-31: Ops-hub low-fi wireframes and API contract review
2026-04-07: Backend scheduler prototype + collision detection running in staging
2026-04-14: First pilot with runtime team for two interleaved rollouts
2026-04-22: Block rollout to customers: Console UI beta and notification flows
acceptance_criteria: Ops-hub displays active canaries for runtime/console/api with owner and impact tags
Scheduler blocks or flags new canaries when cumulative exposure > defined threshold
PagerDuty/Slack notifications are routed to the correct escalation path when overlaps occur
Pilot shows >=40% reduction in duplicate interrupts for participating on-call teams
success_metrics: % reduction in duplicate alerts during multi-rollout windows: target 40%
Time-to-notify correct stakeholder for an overlap incident: target < 5 minutes
Fraction of blocked canaries that result in deferred rollouts vs manual overrides: target >= 70%
Adoption: at least 3 product teams using ops-hub for scheduling in first 6 weeks
risks: Teams may bypass the scheduler if policy is too strict leading to advisory drift
Unexpected edge-cases where dependent canaries must overlap for valid feature flows
Integration surface area with PagerDuty and internal deploy hooks is larger than estimated
UI clutter could reduce clarity unless we iterate on prioritization and filters
